reproduction_target: A population-scale single-cell molecular epidemiology study of 165 self-reported African American adults from the Health among Older Adults Living in Detroit (HOLD) cohort. Wet-lab side: PBMC isolation, overnight starvation culture, 6 h LPS vs vehicle treatment, pooling of 12 donors per batch, 10x Genomics Chromium scRNA-seq (v3.1 Dual index chemistry) and scATAC-seq (Single Cell ATAC kit V2) library preparation, MSD U-PLEX serum cytokine assays, and low-coverage (1x) whole-genome sequencing for genotyping. Computational reproduction target: the FASTQ-to-figure analysis chain - GLIMPSE2 imputation against 1000 Genomes; CellRanger alignment to GRCh38.p12; DIEM debris removal; demuxlet / an unreleased in-house tool 'fastdemux' for donor demultiplexing; Seurat V5 normalisation, 2000 HVGs, 100 PCs, RunHarmony, clustering at dim 13 / resolution 0.15; sctype cell-type annotation with a bespoke cluster-scoring rule; pseudobulk aggregation with 25%-of-columns and >=20-cells filters; DESeq2 differential expression with batch/sex/age/genotype-PC1-2 covariates at 10% BH FDR; ReactomePA over-representation analysis; cellranger-arc alignment of 27 scATAC libraries; ArchR arrow-file QC, addIterativeLSI on 500 bp tiles, addHarmony, addClusters at resolution 0.07, addGeneIntegrationMatrix label transfer with MAGIC imputation; MACS2 peak calling via addReproduciblePeakSet (274,488 peaks); motifmatchr / JASPAR2022 692-core-motif annotation; chromVAR deviation z-scores; per-individual motif-activity averaging with linear-model association testing at 10% FDR; and Fisher's exact-test TF motif enrichment on the DEG sets. No code repository and no data accession of any kind is stated anywhere in the article.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the Methods section of the v1 JATS full text (subsections: Study participants; Psychosocial measures; Cytokine measures / Preprocessing; Circulating Pro-inflammatory Cytokine Composite; Waist-to-Hip ratio; PBMC isolation and culture; PBMC pooling and treatment; scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq sample processing; scRNA-seq raw data processing; Differential gene expression analysis; Pathway enrichment analysis; scATAC-seq raw data processing; Peaks calling for the defined clusters with MACS2; Transcription factors motif analysis; Motif enrichment analysis). The scRNA and scATAC branches are kept separate throughout because they use different aligners (CellRanger vs cellranger-arc), different demultiplexers (demuxlet+fastdemux vs fastdemux only, with an explicitly stated reason) and different clustering frameworks (Seurat vs ArchR). Demultiplexing is kept as its own step in each branch because it is the single point where an undistributed in-house tool enters the chain. Questionnaire/composite-score derivation (C2-C4) is scored as layer C because it is deterministic arithmetic over the collected instrument data, not human adjudication. Wet-lab, assay and sequencing steps are layer W (W = 7) and excluded from S. S = 26.

steps.label: HOLD cohort field protocol: initial home visit and consent, 5-day daily-diary period with saliva sampling and wrist actigraphy, second home visit with anthropometrics/blood pressure/HRV/peak flow/grip strength, and phlebotomist blood draw; 211 participants enrolled, 165 with available PBMCs and DNA selected (data collection November 2017 - March 2020)

Serum cytokine assay: blood in 8.5 mL BD Vacutainer SST (cat. 367988), cryopreserved serum assayed with the Meso Scale Diagnostics U-PLEX Proinflammatory Combo 1 multi-spot system per manufacturer protocol; manufacturer LLODs quoted for 10 analytes
PBMC isolation by Ficoll centrifugation following a previously published protocol (Weckle et al. 2015), cryopreservation in freezing media, liquid-nitrogen storage
Low-coverage (1x) whole-genome sequencing of all individuals for genotyping (library prep, platform and coverage QC not further specified)

PBMC thaw and culture: batches of 12 donors, thaw at 37C, dilution in starvation media (90% RPMI 1640, 10% CS-FBS, 0.1% Gentamycin), Trypan blue counting on Countess II, 400 xg 10 min, 2e6 cells/ml, 100 ul in 2 wells of a 96-well round-bottom plate, ~16 h incubation at 37C / 5% CO2

LPS treatment and pooling: 10 ng/ml LPS or vehicle (water) for 6 h, pooling across individuals into two treatment-specific pools, 300 xg 5 min at 4C, PBS + 0.04% BSA washes, 40 um Flow-Mi filtration, adjustment to 2e6 cells/ml

10x Genomics library preparation and sequencing: scRNA-seq on the Chromium instrument with v3.1 Dual index chemistry; scATAC-seq after DNase treatment and nuclei isolation with Single Cell ATAC kit V2; both per manufacturer protocol

Genotype imputation: 'All individuals in this study were genotyped from low-coverage (1x) whole-genome sequencing and imputed to 37.5 million variants using the 1000 Genomes database as reference and GLIMPSE2 (Rubinacci et al. 2023).' No GLIMPSE2 version, no 1000 Genomes release/build, no chunking or ligation parameters, no post-imputation filters

Cytokine preprocessing: values below the manufacturer LLOD set to 0 (LLODs quoted per analyte); analytes with >40% of samples below LLOD (IL-12p70 42.2%, IL-13 56.8%, IL-1beta 40.5%, IL-2 73.5%, IL-4 69.7%) dropped; remaining analytes (IFN-gamma, IL-10, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-alpha) log10(x+1) transformed and outliers >3 SD winsorised to +/-3 SD

Circulating pro-inflammatory cytokine composite: each cytokine Z-scored, Bartlett's test of sphericity (chi2 = 39.74, p < .001), exploratory factor analysis on the four pro-inflammatory cytokines (IFN-gamma, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-alpha) excluding IL-10, one-factor solution from eigenvalues/scree, loading threshold >0.40, composite = mean of z-scored IFN-gamma, IL-6, TNF-alpha. No software package named for the EFA (extraction method and rotation not stated)

Psychosocial and SES score derivation: ISEL-12 social support (0-3 responses, reverse coding, mean x 12 for a 0-36 mean-imputed sum), 4-item daily-diary Perceived Stress Scale (0-4 responses, reverse coding, per-day mean when all four items answered, then average across available days), SES composite (income 1-13, education 1-12, each Z-scored then averaged), waist-to-hip ratio. Item wording in Tables S1-S2 (supplement PDF, not fetched at stage 1)

scRNA-seq alignment: 'The raw FASTQ files were aligned to the GRCh38.p12 human reference genome using CellRanger.' Reference patch level is pinned (GRCh38.p12) but no CellRanger version, no 10x reference-package build, no cellranger count parameters are given

Ambient/debris droplet removal: 'We eliminated debris-contaminated droplets using the DIEM R package (Alvarez et al. 2020).' No version, no function call, no thresholds or cutoffs, no retained-cell count attributable to this step alone

scRNA-seq donor demultiplexing: 'we tested both demuxlet (Kang et al. 2018) and a new pipeline we developed for this project (fastdemux) using the default parameters, resulting in cell type assignments with high agreement on genotype calls.' fastdemux has no repository, no URL, no version and no preprint; which of the two tools produced the assignments used downstream is not stated. Yield: 558,291 cells across 165 individuals in control and LPS, median 1,703 cells/sample, median 3,981 UMI, 1,760 genes/cell

Seurat preprocessing: 'Seurat (V5) was utilized for preprocessing, clustering, and visualizing the scRNA-seq data' - log normalisation and scaling using Seurat's default method, linear dimensionality reduction on 2,000 highly variable features, 100 principal components. Major version only (V5), no minor/patch, no R version

Batch correction on scRNA-seq: 'We also executed RunHarmony, using the library as a covariate, to correct for library-induced bias (Korsunsky et al. 2019).' No harmony package version, no theta/lambda/iteration settings (defaults implied but not stated)

scRNA-seq clustering and UMAP: clustering run at several resolutions with dimension 50 (default) and dimension 13 (elbow-plot choice); dimension 13 and resolution 0.15 selected for downstream analysis, giving 7 clusters; UMAP applied for visualisation. No random seed, no k.param, no UMAP hyperparameters

Cell-type annotation: 'performed celltyping using sctype (REF) using their immune tissue as a reference' - the citation is literally the unreplaced placeholder '(REF)'. A bespoke resolution-selection rule follows (per-cell-type score sums, top major-type assignment, proportion of correct assignments per cluster, weighted by cluster_size/total_cells), yielding 6 major PBMC cell types. No sctype version, no marker-database version or download date, no score thresholds

Pseudobulk construction: per cluster and treatment, sum all cells of each individual/sample into a gene-by-sample matrix; keep genes expressed in 25% of the columns; remove columns (samples) with fewer than 20 cells in the cluster

Differential expression: 'We performed differential gene expression analysis for each variable, treatment and cell type separately using R DESeq2 package (Love, Huber, and Anders 2014)', covariates batch, sex, age, genotype PC1 and PC2; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR applied per run; DEGs at 10% FDR; separate LPS-versus-CTRL contrast model with the same covariates. Results quoted: 1,956 stress DEGs and 1,296 social-support DEGs. No DESeq2 version, no R version, no design-formula text, no shrinkage/fitType/test settings

Pathway over-representation analysis: 'Over-representation analysis (ORA) was done in ReactomePA using the Reactome pathways implemented in enrichPathway (Yu et al. 2012)', run separately for stress-upregulated and support-downregulated genes per cell type, concatenated across cell types and variables, filtered at 10% FDR, ordered by frequency; top 4 pathways shown in Figure 3B. No ReactomePA version, no Reactome database release or snapshot date, no gene universe/background definition, no min/max gene-set size

scATAC-seq alignment: 'We aligned reads for ATAC-seq data from 27 libraries by running cellranger-arc with the human reference genome (GRCh 38)'; 'For quality control, we used default settings for cellranger-arc and ArchR steps.' Build named without patch level, no cellranger-arc version, no reference-package version

scATAC-seq donor demultiplexing: 'we demultiplexed and assigned the individual identity for each cell with fastdemux. Fastdemux was selected over demuxlet due to demuxlet limitation on runtime and handling of the large number of scATAC reads.' The sole demultiplexer for this branch is the undistributed in-house tool; no repository, URL, version or parameters. Singlets with correct individual/batch matching retained; 400,535 cells remain

ArchR project construction and QC: create arrow files from fragment files (QC, genome-wide tile matrix, gene score matrix, stored as HDF5 on disk), then create the ArchRProject; 'we used default settings for cellranger-arc and ArchR steps'. No ArchR version, no explicit TSS-enrichment or nFrags cutoffs, no genome annotation package version

Iterative LSI dimensionality reduction: addIterativeLSI on the genome-wide 500 bp tile matrix with default settings - LSI on the most accessible tiles in a subset, projection of all cells, Seurat SNN clustering, variable-feature identification, second iteration repeating steps 1-2; LSI components correlating with sequencing depth above 0.75 (default) excluded. No ArchR version, no seed, no varFeatures/iteration count beyond 'second iterative'

scATAC batch correction: 'We applied the Harmony algorithm to correct batch effects by running addHarmony with the groupBy setting to be library.' No package version, no non-default Harmony parameters stated

scATAC clustering and UMAP: 'We clustered cells using addClusters with the 0.07 resolution', graph-based clustering delegated to Seurat; UMAP for visualisation; 10 main clusters identified at resolution 0.07. No seed, no UMAP hyperparameters, no dimensions-used specification

scRNA-to-scATAC label transfer: addGeneIntegrationMatrix performing parallel FindTransferAnchors alignments over divided cell subsets; gene scores inferred from chromatin accessibility with the default ArchR gene score model and MAGIC imputation; RNA labels at resolution 0.15 transferred to ATAC and a confusion matrix computed against the ATAC clusters. No subset sizes, no anchor parameters, no MAGIC settings, no seed, no package versions

Peak calling: MACS2 invoked through the ArchR addReproduciblePeakSet function for the 10 clusters at resolution 0.07, using the iterative-overlap approach (Corces et al. 2018); a robust peak set of 274,488 features; insertion counts quantified with addPeakMatrix; peaks annotated to the closest hg38 gene within 100 kb. No MACS2 version beyond the tool name, no q-value/extsize/shift settings, no pseudo-replicate or reproducibility parameters

TF motif annotation: addMotifAnnotations wrapping matchMotifs from motifmatchr to build a TF-occupancy matrix over the robust peak set, restricted to 'the 692 core motifs from the JASPAR2022 (Castro-Mondragon et al. 2022)'. Motif database release is pinned (JASPAR2022) and the motif count is given; no motifmatchr version, no p-value cutoff for motif matching

TF motif activity: chromVAR run through addDeviationsMatrix to compute deviations between genome-wide accessibility of peaks carrying a TF motif (sex chromosomes excluded) and the expected value, corrected with background peak sets (Schep et al. 2017); z-scores (deviation/standard error) carried downstream. No chromVAR version, no background-peak count, no seed

Motif-activity association testing: motif activity averaged over cells of the same individual, cell type and treatment to give a motif-by-individual matrix per treatment and cell type; linear model associating TF activity with each psychosocial factor separately, with top 2 genotype PCs, gender, age and batch as confounders; differentially active motifs (DAM) defined at less than 10% FDR 'derived from p.adjust with Benjamini-Hochberg bonferroni correction' - two mutually exclusive corrections named in one clause. No R version, no model-fitting function named, no handling of the treatment factor stated

Motif enrichment on DEGs: TF-regulated gene sets built from (1) peaks bound by the TF in the TF-occupancy matrix, restricted per cell type to peaks measured in at least 1% of cells, and (2) the genes closest to those peaks; two Fisher's exact tests per cell type and psychosocial factor - a per-TF enrichment test and an overall test of whether DEGs are enriched in DAMs. No multiple-testing correction stated for the per-TF tests, no contingency-table construction detail, no software named

headline.static_readiness: 0/26 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 0/26 (0%) steps reach RI at stage 1. The binding constraint is a single global one: the data axis is 0 for every computational step, because the article contains no Data Availability statement and no accession of any kind (no GEO, SRA, ENA, ArrayExpress, dbGaP, EGA, figshare, Zenodo or Dryad identifier appears anywhere in the full text) for the scRNA-seq FASTQ, the scATAC-seq FASTQ, the low-coverage WGS/imputed genotypes, the serum cytokine measurements or the psychosocial questionnaire scores. Since RI requires all four axes >= 1 simultaneously, no step can clear RI regardless of how well the parameters are described - and many of them are described well (C8, C12, C13, C18, C23, C24, C26 all reach params = 2). The second constraint is code: there is no Code Availability statement and no repository, so the code axis is at best 1 (reconstructable from prose) and drops to 0 at C7 and C16, where the only demultiplexer used for the ATAC branch is an in-house tool named 'fastdemux' that is described as 'a new pipeline we developed for this project' with no URL, no version and no accompanying preprint; those two steps are scored X and they sit upstream of every ATAC result in the paper. Version evidence is thin: only three steps carry any version identifier at all (C5 GRCh38.p12, C8/C10 Seurat V5, C23 JASPAR2022), and all three are resource or major-version mentions rather than software pins, so capture_claim is 'floating' and the paper is not a stage-2 candidate.
headline.coverage: 33 steps built from the Methods section of the v1 JATS XML (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/early/2025/10/15/2025.10.14.682318.source.xml, fetched 200 OK, 147,170 bytes, title phrase 'opposing single-cell pro-inflammatory' confirmed present). 7 are wet-lab/assay/sequencing steps scored OOS (W = 7); 26 are computational (S = 26). The article has no Data Availability section, no Code Availability section and no Methods subsection covering software environment; the only availability-flavoured statements in the document are the CC BY-NC-ND licence line, the Competing Interest statement ('The authors have declared no competing interest') and the Acknowledgments funding list. One supplementary PDF (supplements/682318_file02.pdf, containing Tables S1-S4 and Figures S1-S8) is listed but was not fetched at stage 1; questionnaire item wording (C4) and the cell-type/cluster tables live there.

gaps.missing: The article states no code repository of any kind. There is no Code Availability statement, no Data Availability statement, and no GitHub / GitLab / Bitbucket / Zenodo / Software Heritage / OSF identifier anywhere in the full text (a full-text scan of the v1 JATS XML returns URLs only for the Creative Commons licence, an ORCID record and six ROR institution identifiers). No alignment script, no Seurat or ArchR analysis script, no DESeq2 model script, no ReactomePA script, no chromVAR or linear-model association script, and no figure-generation code exists for a reproducer to run. Every step in the chain must be re-implemented from prose.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the full analysis code (scRNA branch, scATAC branch, association testing and figure generation) in a public repository, archive a tagged release to Zenodo for a citable DOI, and add a Code Availability statement pointing at that DOI.

gaps.missing: No accession is stated for any dataset the paper generated: the scRNA-seq FASTQ (558,291 cells, 165 donors, control and LPS), the scATAC-seq FASTQ (27 libraries, 400,535 cells), the low-coverage 1x whole-genome sequencing reads and the resulting 37.5-million-variant imputed genotypes, the MSD serum cytokine readouts, and the HOLD psychosocial/anthropometric measures. The article carries no Data Availability section at all, so there is not even a controlled-access route named (no dbGaP phs, no EGA study, no institutional DAC contact). The data are human, identifiable-adjacent (genotypes plus a named small geographic cohort of self-reported African American Detroit residents aged 50-89), so controlled access would be the expected route - but the absence is total, not a controlled-access designation.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit raw reads and genotypes under a controlled-access repository (dbGaP or EGA) with a stated accession and DAC contact, deposit derived non-identifiable matrices (per-cell-type pseudobulk counts, peak matrices, motif-activity matrices, de-identified psychosocial scores) in an open repository such as GEO, and add a Data Availability statement naming every accession.

gaps.where: Article-level metadata - absence of an availability statement
gaps.missing: bioRxiv v1 carries no Data Availability and no Code Availability heading. The JATS section list is: Competing Interest Statement, Introduction, Results (5 subsections), Discussion, Methods (15 subsections), Supporting information, Acknowledgments, References. The Acknowledgments name funders (R01GM109215, R01HL153377, P30AG015281, P50MD017351, P30ES020957 pilot, CZI Ancestry Networks) and disclose that 'AI tools were used to edit portions of the initial draft of the manuscript', but say nothing about artifact deposition. A reproducer therefore has no address to write to and no statement to hold the authors to.
gaps.how_to_close: Add explicit Data Availability and Code Availability statements at submission, even if the answer is controlled access, and register the controlled-access study before posting the preprint.

gaps.where: Whole analysis environment - both the R/Bioconductor stack and the 10x command-line stack
gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, container image, image digest, conda/mamba environment file, renv.lock, requirements.txt or session_info dump is mentioned. The R version is never stated, and the analysis spans at least a dozen interacting R/Bioconductor packages (Seurat, harmony, DIEM, DESeq2, ReactomePA, ArchR, motifmatchr, chromVAR, Rmagic/MAGIC) plus two 10x command-line pipelines (CellRanger, cellranger-arc) plus GLIMPSE2 and MACS2. Nothing in the article constrains which build of any of these produced the reported numbers.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock/renv.lock or a container image referenced by digest that covers the whole chain, and record sessionInfo() output alongside the results.

gaps.where: Software version pinning across all computational steps; and the in-house tool 'fastdemux' (C7, C16)
gaps.missing: Not one software version number of the form X.Y or X.Y.Z appears anywhere in the article. Tools are named without any version: CellRanger, cellranger-arc, DIEM, demuxlet, harmony/RunHarmony, sctype, DESeq2, ReactomePA/enrichPathway, ArchR, motifmatchr, chromVAR, MAGIC, and R itself. Three mentions look like versions but are not software pins: 'GLIMPSE2' and 'MACS2' are the tools' names, 'Seurat (V5)' is a major version only. The in-house tool fastdemux is the worst case - it is 'a new pipeline we developed for this project', it is the sole demultiplexer for the entire scATAC branch, and it has no repository, no version, no license and no preprint, so steps C7 and C16 cannot be attempted at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Record exact versions (package version plus, for the 10x pipelines, the reference-package build) for every named tool in Methods, and release fastdemux publicly with a version tag and an archived DOI before it is relied upon in a published analysis.

gaps.where: External reference resources: C1 (1000 Genomes), C5/C15 (human genome reference), C11 (sctype marker database), C14 (Reactome), C23 (JASPAR2022)
gaps.missing: External resource pinning is inconsistent. Adequately identified: the scRNA reference is given as 'GRCh38.p12' (patch level stated) and the motif set as 'the 692 core motifs from the JASPAR2022'. Unpinned: the 1000 Genomes imputation reference has no phase/release identifier; the scATAC reference is only 'GRCh 38' with no patch level and no 10x reference-package version, so it may or may not be the same reference used for the RNA branch; the sctype immune-tissue marker database has no version or download date and its citation is an unreplaced '(REF)' placeholder; the Reactome pathway database consumed by enrichPathway has no release number or snapshot date, which alone can shift the ORA results reported in Figure 3B. All of these are stage-1 prose observations; env_capture_class is 'n/a' throughout because there is no code to inspect.
gaps.how_to_close: State the release identifier and retrieval date for every external database (1000 Genomes phase/release, the exact 10x reference package for both branches, the sctype marker-table version, the Reactome release), and obtain them inside the workflow from versioned URLs with recorded checksums.

gaps.where: C25 (motif-activity association testing) and C11 (cell-type annotation citation)
gaps.missing: Two internal inconsistencies that a reproducer cannot resolve from the text. (1) C25 states that DAMs are 'defined as those with less than 10% FDR derived from p.adjust with Benjamini-Hochberg bonferroni correction' - Benjamini-Hochberg and Bonferroni are different corrections with different acceptance sets, and the FDR framing fits only the former; which was actually applied determines the DAM count that Figures 4-6 rest on. (2) C11's cell-typing tool is cited as 'sctype (REF)' - the reference placeholder was never replaced, so the tool cannot be resolved to a specific implementation (ScType has more than one distributed form) or to its marker database.
gaps.how_to_close: Correct the multiple-testing sentence to name a single procedure and report the corrected-p threshold actually used, and replace the '(REF)' placeholder with the intended citation and package identity.

gaps.where: Method description / run order and figure provenance
gaps.missing: There is no run-order documentation and no mapping from Methods steps to the reported figures and tables. The two branches interleave (the scRNA clustering at resolution 0.15 is an input to the scATAC label transfer in C21), and the association analyses in C25/C26 consume outputs of both branches, but the dependency graph is only implicit in the prose ordering. No step-to-figure mapping is given for Figures 1-6 or Figures S1-S8, and no intermediate artifact (pseudobulk matrices, DEG tables, peak set, motif-activity matrix, DAM list) is deposited, so a reproducer cannot check partial progress against anything.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a workflow (Snakemake/Nextflow or a numbered script sequence) that encodes the dependency order, and deposit the intermediate matrices and result tables keyed to the figure each one produces.

gaps.missing: No gap in the computational sense - recorded for completeness. Participant recruitment and the HOLD field protocol, serum cytokine assay on the MSD U-PLEX platform, Ficoll PBMC isolation, low-coverage WGS, PBMC thaw/culture, LPS treatment and donor pooling, and 10x Chromium scRNA-seq (v3.1 Dual index) / Single Cell ATAC V2 library preparation are physical procedures and are out of scope for computational reproduction (scored OOS, excluded from S). They are described at protocol level with reagent catalogue numbers and concentrations, which is adequate for wet-lab replication; the biological material itself (cryopreserved PBMCs from a closed 2017-2020 cohort) is not obtainable by a third party.
gaps.how_to_close: n/a - out of scope. The computational reproduction route for a third party runs from deposited raw reads, which is covered by gap type 1.
